native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: The advantage in BA-completion rates for Black students is most pronounced at the highest socioeconomic level. In the NLS sample Black students complete below White students overall and across all low- and middle-SES quintiles (Black 0.2-2.2% vs White 1.3-4.2%), but the Black-White gap steadily narrows with SES and effectively closes at the top: in the top SES quintile Black completion (7/203 = 3.45%) essentially equals White (50/1416 = 3.53%), and in the top SES decile Black completion (5/82 = 6.10%) is the highest of any group, exceeding White (36/737 = 4.88%) and Hispanic (2/58 = 3.45%). This high-SES advantage is robust in direction - in a logistic model adjusting for ASVAB ability, class percentile and sex, the Black x top-SES interaction is the largest positive effect (OR ~8, p ~0.07) and holds even though high-SES Black students have lower mean ability than high-SES White students (ASVAB ~1945 vs ~2224). Stated plainly, the top-level advantage rests on few completions (5 of 82 Black students in the top decile, SE ~ +/-2.6 pp; 7 of 203 in the top quintile, SE ~ +/-1.3 pp), so the point estimate is imprecise and its CI includes zero: the defensible conclusion is that the Black-White completion gap is at its smallest - effectively closed and modestly positive in the raw data - precisely at the highest SES level, which is where any Black-student advantage is concentrated.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load data/nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8773, 0 missing); confirm SES is a continuous standardized-ish score (mean -0.009, std 0.742, range -2.445..2.718) and BA DEGREE COMPLETED a clean binary. 2) Define completion rate = mean(BA DEGREE COMPLETED); overall 2.69% (White 3.54%, Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%). 3) Segment SES into quintiles (primary) and deciles (robustness) via quantile cuts. 4) For each SES bin compute Black vs White (primary comparator), Black vs Hispanic, and Black vs overall-mean completion gaps in pp plus ratios, reporting per-cell N and raw counts (s/n) and a Wald SE for the Black cell. 5) Identify the SES level where the Black advantage is largest/positive. 6) Sensitivity (not in headline): fit logistic regression completion ~ SES-quintile + race + SES-quintile:race + ASVAB ability + class percentile + sex to test whether the high-SES Black advantage survives covariate adjustment (it does, directionally; Black x top-SES is the largest positive interaction, OR~8, p~0.07). Concluded the advantage is most pronounced at the highest SES level, with the caveat that the top-cell estimate is imprecise.

sub_hypo.relations: The Black × top-SES-quintile interaction is the largest positive interaction in the adjusted logistic model (OR approximately 8, p approximately 0.07), supporting the advantage directionally rather than establishing a precise effect.

sub_hypo.text: High-SES Black students show the completion advantage despite having lower mean ASVAB ability than high-SES White students.
sub_hypo.context: High-SES Black and White students in the NLS sample.
